item.title: Ramified convolution and monodromy bases for symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.29051v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We realize the positive enveloping algebra of a symmetrizable Kac--Moody algebra by convolution on a ramified preprojective species over $\mathbb{C}((t))$. The coefficients are alternating traces of tame monodromy on representation flag varieties. We prove the relative Serre relations modulo classes induced from proper finite extensions. Monodromy evaluations at compatible generic points of the central reductions yield an integral basis respecting the top and socle crystals. The basis is unchanged by scaling the symmetrizer, induces bases of integrable representation lattices, and agrees with Lusztig's semicanonical basis when the Cartan matrix is symmetric. We prove the acyclic convolution conjecture of Gei\ss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer for all symmetrizable Cartan matrices and all positive integral symmetrizers. Finally, we give a counterexample to the Support Conjecture of Gei\ss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer and compute a ramified lift for which monodromy restores the Serre relation.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei

item.title: Frobenius forms and semisimplicity of cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.29403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the Nakayama automorphism of the canonical homogeneous Frobenius form on cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras. We give explicit necessary and sufficient conditions on the dominant weight and the rank for semisimplicity of cyclotomic quiver Hecke superalgebras of types $A_e^{(1)}$, $C_e^{(1)}$, $A_{2e}^{(2)}$, $D_{e+1}^{(2)}$, $A_\infty$, $B_\infty$, and $C_\infty$. As an application, we prove that a cyclotomic Hecke--Clifford superalgebra is semisimple if and only if the corresponding Poincar\'e polynomial is nonzero.
item.dc:creator: Shuo Li, Lei Shi

item.title: Enhanced Langlands Parameters of Regular Principal Series
item.description: arXiv:2610.29471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe the enhanced Langlands parameters of the irreducible constituents of a regular principal series of a quasi-split reductive group over a non-archimedean local field of characteristic zero. Starting from the chamber parametrization by Rodier and Luo, we determine the monodromy of each constituent and show that its enhancement is trivial. In particular, we obtain the corresponding parameter of the unique irreducible subrepresentation.
item.dc:creator: Haoming Li, Xiaohang Yang, Jizhi Zhang, Yelei Zhao

item.title: Revisiting the infinite Galois correspondence via group representations
item.description: arXiv:2610.29480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inspired by Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem, we interpret the Galois correspondence as a special case of a simple general principle in harmonic analysis on profinite groups. This also gives a representation-theoretic characterisation of profinite groups.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Chen, Enxin Wu

item.title: Local Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture for unitary groups: Trace formula approach for epsilon dichotomy
item.description: arXiv:2610.29483v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The purpose of this paper is to provide a proof independent of the theta-lifting for the epsilon-dichotomy of the local Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture of real unitary groups for tempered L-parameters. The approach is based on the local trace formula and endoscopic character identities following Waldspurger and Chen-Luo.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Chen, Xiaowei Li, Bushi Ren

item.title: Homological branching laws for $p$-adic and mod $p$ representations of ${\rm GL}_2$ over a $p$-adic field
item.description: arXiv:2610.29629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ and $p\geq 5$. In this paper, we establish homological branching laws for mod $p$ representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ restricted to split and nonsplit maximal tori, treating principal and special series and, when $F=\mathbb Q_p$, supersingular representations. We determine the derived Hom-complexes in both orders for nonexceptional characters. At exceptional characters, we calculate their Euler--Poincar\'e characteristics under a $p$-torsion-freeness hypothesis. We also establish corresponding results for a class of unitary Banach space representations.
item.dc:creator: Yang Chen, Haoran Wang

item.title: Restriction of $p'$-degree characters, fields of values, and relative normal complements
item.description: arXiv:2610.29672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a finite $p$-solvable group for a prime $p$, and let $P$ be a Sylow $p$-subgroup of $G$. Centella and Navarro proved that there is a canonical bijection ${\rm Irr}_{p'}(\Phi_{1_G})\to{\rm Irr}_{p'}(\Phi_{1_{\textbf N_G(P)}})$ preserving fields of values, where $\Phi_{1_G}$ denotes the principal projective indecomposable character of $G$. In the spirit of a result of Berkovich on the McKay bijection, we characterize when this projective correspondence can be realized by restriction, proving that it holds if and only if $\mathbf{N}_G(P)$ admits a certain relative normal complement in $G$. More generally, we establish a refined criterion incorporating fields of values, and we extend this characterization to $\pi$-separable groups with nilpotent Hall $\pi$-subgroups.
item.dc:creator: David Cabrera-Berenguer

item.title: On Lusztig Sheaves for Tame Quivers
item.description: arXiv:2610.29750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $Q$ be a connected quiver of tame type, and let $U_v^-$ be the positive part of the corresponding quantized affine algebra. In Lusztig's construction of the canonical basis of $U_v^-$, the simple perverse sheaves occurring, up to shift, as direct summands of the flag sheaf complexes are given by intersection cohomology complexes $\operatorname{IC}(X(c,m),\mathcal{L}_{\chi})$. We study the restrictions of these intersection cohomology complexes to the locally closed subsets $Y(c,m)$ obtained by fixing the preprojective, non-homogeneous regular, and preinjective summands in the category $\operatorname{rep} Q$. We prove pointwise purity on the loci where the homogeneous regular part is a direct sum of pairwise non-isomorphic quasi-simple modules, and establish a semisimple decomposition of the restrictions to the corresponding larger strata. The graded multiplicities of the local systems associated with irreducible characters of symmetric groups determine the transition coefficients from the canonical basis to the PBW basis constructed via quiver representations. This gives a geometric explanation of the positivity of these coefficients and the unitriangularity of the transition matrix.
item.dc:creator: Yumeng Wu, Jie Xiao

item.title: On unitary vertex operator algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.29878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that a conformal vertex algebra with a non-zero invariant Hermitian form is unitary as soon as it admits a non-zero positive energy module with a positive definite invariant Hermitian form. Using free field realizations, we deduce that the principal simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g)$ of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ is unitary for central charge $c\ge rank(\mathfrak g)+24\bigl((\rho|\rho^\vee)+\|\rho\|\,\|\rho^\vee\|\bigr)$, and, if $\mathfrak g$ is simply laced, for all $c\ge rank(\mathfrak g)$. Among basic Lie superalgebras which are not Lie algebras, the free field argument applies to $osp(1|2n)$ and $osp(2|2n)$. It shows that $W_k(osp(1|2n))$ is unitary for $c\ge n+\frac12$ and gives an explicit bound for $osp(2|2n)$. Next, we prove that if $\mathfrak s$ is an even $sl_2$-subalgebra of a simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ whose centralizer is not abelian, then the simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak s)$ is unitary for at most finitely many $k$. We illustrate this on the $W$-algebras of $sl_{qm}$ attached to the nilpotents of Jordan type $q^m$: unitarity is possible only at two levels, and for $q=2$ it does occur at both. For instance, the $W$-algebra of $sl_4$ attached to the partition $2+2$ is unitary only for $k=-2$ and $k=-\frac32$. This fails for Lie superalgebras, as minimal $W$-algebras show, but still holds under stronger assumptions. Finally, we prove that a simple $W$-algebra $W_k(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak s)$ can be unitary for only finitely many $k$ if $\mathfrak g$ is a simple Lie algebra and $\mathfrak s$ is not a distinguished $sl_2$ subalgebra.
item.dc:creator: Victor G. Kac, Pierluigi M\"oseneder Frajria, Paolo Papi

item.title: Mackey formulas for smooth stacks
item.description: arXiv:2610.29970v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study parabolic induction and restriction functors on derived categories of constructible sheaves, D-modules, and other sheaf theories on smooth stacks with good or adequate moduli spaces. We prove a commutation rule between them in the form of a Mackey filtration, indexed by the set of relative positions of two elements in the component lattice, a combinatorial structure that characterizes inductions and restrictions on a given stack. This generalizes similar results for adjoint quotient stacks studied in generalized Springer theory and the theory of character sheaves, and for stacks of quiver representations appearing in Lusztig's categorification of quantum groups. We also apply our result to the stack of semistable principal bundles on a curve, as a first step towards Mackey formulas in geometric Langlands correspondences.
item.dc:creator: Chenjing Bu, Lucien Hennecart

item.title: Characters and Polynomiality for Maximal Parabolic Unipotent Radicals in Finite Classical Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.29976v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Characters and Polynomiality for Maximal Parabolic Unipotent Radicals in Finite Classical GroupsLet $q$ be a power of an odd prime. For the unipotent radicals of maximal rational parabolic subgroups of the finite symplectic, orthogonal and unitary groups, we determine all complex irreducible characters, their values, and the number of characters of each degree. Each of these numbers is a polynomial in $q-1$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, in analogy with a conjecture of Isaacs for unitriangular groups. For the orthogonal radicals, the character table and the power maps do not depend on the Witt type of the residual form, whereas the isomorphism type of the radical does when the isotropic dimension is at least three and the residual dimension is positive and even. Consequently, for $3\le a\le n-1$ the radicals of the stabilizers of totally isotropic $a$-spaces in $\SO^+_{2n}(q)$ and $\SO^-_{2n}(q)$ form Brauer pairs; for $a\le n-2$ both stabilizers are maximal parabolic subgroups. Finally, we express the multiplicities through $R$-polynomials, with the unequal parameters $q^2,\dots,q^2,q$ in the unitary case.
item.dc:creator: Qingchun Hao, Yang Yang

item.title: Reflection functors for non-simply-laced quiver varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.30065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the braid relations between reflection functors on non-simply-laced analogues of Nakajima quiver varieties, which are defined as critical loci of certain quivers with potential. We extend this framework to categories of matrix factorizations and critical $K$-theory.
item.dc:creator: Andrei Negu\c{t}

item.title: Closedness of bounded strength and partition rank loci
item.description: arXiv:2610.28792v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show the existence of a quartic form of strength $3$ in the closure of the strength at most $2$ locus, answering a question of Ballico--Bik--Oneto--Ventura in the negative. In the analogous setting of partition rank as introduced by Naslund, we further show that the locus of tensors of partition rank at most $2$ is closed, but the locus of tensors of partition rank at most $3$ is not. Together with a suspension lemma, this answers for all $r$ whether the locus of forms/tensors of strength/partition rank at most $r$ is Zariski-closed.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Baily, Alessandro Danelon

item.title: No braiding for quantum sl2 reps - A short proof
item.description: arXiv:2610.29748v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a short and self-contained proof that the category of all finite dimensional representations of quantum sl2 is not braided.
item.dc:creator: Liao Wang, Zbigniew Wojciechowski

item.title: Lax descent and foliated Verdier duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.29977v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Higher categorical methods allow us to view recollements as lax descent data and build a corresponding descent theory governed by an $\infty$-bicategorical theory of limits. We demonstrate some concrete innovations brought along by these new techniques in the classical context of constructible and perverse sheaves on stratified spaces. Our first application uses partially (op)lax descent to recover the famous result of Beilinson telling us how to glue perverse sheaves in terms of vanishing and nearby cycles. The remainder of the article is concerened with establishing a uniform view on a series of classification results for perverse sheaves culminating in recent work of Kapranov-Schechtman. Namely, we use lax descent to establish a ``foliated'' variant of Verdier duality which, informally speaking, identifies the derived constructible category of a suitably foliated space with sections of a categorical cosheaf on the leaf space whose stalks are the categories of sheaves along the leaves. Again, this is obtained as an application of lax descent, and seems to provide a reasonable framework to formalize the idea of ``mixed sheaf-cosheaf objects'' promoted by Kapranov and Schechtman.
item.dc:creator: Tobias Dyckerhoff, Till Heine, Simon Schneider, Kostiantyn Tolmachov

item.title: Multiplying matrices via polynomials: exposition and barriers
item.description: arXiv:2610.30054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give an exposition of OpenAI's recent proof that the exponent $\omega_\mathbb{C}$ of matrix multiplication over the complex numbers satisfies $\omega_\mathbb{C}\leq9/4$. Our version of the proof gives $\omega_\mathbb{F}\leq9/4$ over every field $\mathbb{F}$. We also treat the rectangular matrix multiplication exponent $\omega_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)$. Here we have $\omega_\mathbb{F}(1,k,1)=2$ for $0\leq k\leq1/2$ and $\omega_\mathbb{F}(1,k,1)\leq1+k+1/(4k)$ for $k\geq1/2$, and, for real numbers $a\geq b\geq c\geq0$, $\omega_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)=a+b$ if $c(a+b)\leq ab$ and $\omega_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)\leq(a+b+c)/2+(ab/c+ac/b+bc/a)/4$ otherwise. Our exposition is in the language of degeneration inequalities among polynomial multiplication tensors and Strassen's asymptotic spectrum duality. We moreover prove an operational barrier (which can be thought of as coming from an operational asymptotic spectrum) showing that the current analysis of all these upper bounds on $\omega_\mathbb{F}$ and $\omega_\mathbb{F}(a,b,c)$ is optimal and that in fact the current degeneration ingredients cannot improve the bounds.
item.dc:creator: Alimzhan Amanov, Maxim van den Berg, Jeroen Zuiddam

item.title: Gelfand-Kirillov dimensions and annihilator varieties of highest weight modules of exceptional Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2509.24346v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $L(\lambda)$ be an irreducible highest weight module of a complex simple Lie algebra of exceptional type, with highest weight $\lambda-\rho$, where $\rho$ is half the sum of positive roots. Its annihilator variety is the closure of a nilpotent orbit of dimension twice the Gelfand--Kirillov (GK) dimension of $L(\lambda)$. We develop an explicit algorithm that determines both invariants for any infinitesimal character. The GK dimension is reduced to evaluating Lusztig's $\mathbf{a}$-function on the integral Weyl group of $\lambda$. After decomposing the integral root system into irreducible factors, classical factors are treated by the Robinson--Schensted insertion algorithm and the H-algorithm, while exceptional factors are handled by positive index reduction and PyCox. The annihilator orbit is then recovered from the local special datum by Springer theory and Sommers duality. An implementation is available online and takes $\lambda$ as input to compute the GK dimension and annihilator variety of $L(\lambda)$.
item.dc:creator: Zhanqiang Bai, Fan Gao, Yutong Wang, Xun Xie

item.title: Weights and characters for affine Hecke algebras
item.description: arXiv:2607.10010v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Weights play an essential role in the classification of simple modules for affine Hecke algebras. In this paper we show the extent to which weights determine simple modules and relate this to induction and restriction along isogenies. We also describe the behaviour of hermitian duals and unitarity under induction and restriction along isogenies.
item.dc:creator: Maximilien J. Mackie

item.title: Categorification of the genus two DAHA
item.description: arXiv:2608.13278v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct three derived endofunctors on the derived category of graded integrable representations of the current algebra of a flat degeneration of $D(2|1,\alpha)$, and prove that their classes in the Grothendieck group are the genus two Macdonald operators. Computing the graded $\operatorname{Ext}$ pairing explicitly, we deduce the self-adjointness of the genus two Macdonald operators and the orthogonality of genus $2$ Macdonald polynomials with respect to the certain skew-bilinear form.
item.dc:creator: Semeon Arthamonov, Ievgen Makedonskyi, Daniil Sarafannikov

item.title: Classification of $U(\mathfrak h)$-Free Modules over the Heisenberg-Virasoro type Lie superalgebra via Polynomial Shift Operators
item.description: arXiv:2609.32105v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let \(\mathcal L\) be the Heisenberg-Virasoro type Lie superalgebra whose even part is the twisted Heisenberg-Virasoro algebra and whose odd part is an abelian ideal. We classify \(\mathbb Z_2\)-graded \(\mathcal L\)-modules that are free of super-rank \(1|1\) over \(U(\mathfrak h)=\mathbb C[L_0,F_0]\). Using polynomial shift operators, we express the defining relations as functional equations for the matrix entries of the generators. Assuming the rank one classification for the even subalgebra, we show that, up to parity reversal, every module with nontrivial odd action belongs to a triangular family \(\Omega^+(\lambda,\beta,d)\), whereas every module with trivial odd action is a direct sum of two rank-one modules for the even subalgebra. We determine the graded isomorphism classes: within the triangular family, the coupling polynomial \(d\) is invariant up to multiplication by a non-zero scalar. We also describe canonical proper submodules and show that every module in the classification is reducible. In particular, we provide a new realization of the Heisenberg-Virasoro type Lie superalgebra using $2\times2$ matrices with entries associated with polynomial shift-differential operators.
item.dc:creator: Yan Kong, Haibo Chen, Yucai Su

item.title: Approximability of Triangulated Categories under Separable Extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.27031v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the behavior of approximability under separable extensions of triangulated categories. Let $\mathcal{B}$ be an approximable triangulated category and let $\mathbf{T}=(T,\theta,\mu)$ be a smashing, stably separable exact monad on $\mathcal{B}$. Assume that the category of $\mathbf{T}$-modules $\mathbf{T}\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathcal{B}}$ admits a canonical triangulated structure. We prove that if $T$ is right $t$-exact with respect to a $t$-structure in the preferred equivalence class of $\mathcal{B}$, then $\mathbf{T}\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}_{\mathcal{B}}$ is again an approximable triangulated category. As an application, we show that, under suitable assumptions, a smashing localization functor on an approximable triangulated category induces a recollement of approximable triangulated categories, thereby yielding a converse-type result to the gluing theorem of Burke--Neeman--Pauwels. Finally, under suitable hypotheses, we prove that separable extensions restrict naturally to the intrinsic subcategories associated with approximable triangulated categories.
item.dc:creator: Mengzhen Zhu, Yuefei Zheng, Xianhui Fu

item.title: Spectral mod p Satake isomorphism for GL_n
item.description: arXiv:2402.14011v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $K/\mathbb{Q}_p$ be a finite extension with residue field $k$. By a work of Emerton--Gee, irreducible components inside the reduced special fiber of the moduli stack of rank $n$ \'etale $(\varphi,\Gamma)$-modules are labeled by Serre weights of $\mathrm{GL}_n(k)$. Let $\sigma$ be a non-Steinberg Serre weight and $\mathcal{C}_\sigma$ be the corresponding irreducible component. Motivated by the categorical $p$-adic local Langlands program, we construct a natural injective map $\mathcal{O}(\mathcal{C}_\sigma) \hookrightarrow \mathcal{H}(\sigma)$ from the ring of global functions on $\mathcal{C}_\sigma$ to the Hecke algebra of $\sigma$ compatible with the mod $p$ Satake isomorphism by Herzig and Henniart--Vign\'eras in a suitable sense. For sufficiently generic $\sigma$, we prove that it is an isomorphism. As an application, we obtain a natural stratification of the irreducible component whose strata are equipped with a parabolic structure. Our main input is a construction of a morphism from an integral Hecke algebra of a generic tame type to the ring of global functions on a tamely potentially crystalline Emerton--Gee stack.
item.dc:creator: Heejong Lee

item.title: Partial actions of groups on monoidal categories
item.description: arXiv:2412.13123v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we introduce the notion of a partial action of a group on a strict monoidal category. We propose, in the context of Monoidal categories, new constructions analogous to those existing for partial group actions over an algebra such as the globalization, the subalgebra of partial invariants, and the partial smash product.
item.dc:creator: Eliezer Batista, Felipe Lopes Castro, Mykola Khrypchenko

item.title: Central series of cocommutative Hopf braces
item.description: arXiv:2605.03798v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: By extending some classical results known for groups and skew braces, we define and investigate central series of cocommutative Hopf braces. Both left and right central series are defined using a $\star$-product that measures the difference between the two algebra operations, and naturally leads to introducing the notions of socle and of annihilator of a cocommutative Hopf brace. We characterize the central extensions relative to the subcategories of cocommutative Hopf algebras and of commutative and cocommutative Hopf algebras, respectively. Since the category of cocommutative Hopf braces is semi-abelian and it has enough projectives with respect to the class of cleft extensions, one can then establish suitable Hopf formulae for their homology. These are expressed in terms of the corresponding notions of relative commutators of cocommutative Hopf braces. In particular, the one relative to the subcategory of commutative and cocommutative Hopf algebras turns out to be the Huq commutator.
item.dc:creator: Maria Bevilacqua, Marino Gran, Andrea Sciandra
